sun.upright:
Walking away from a fight you could probably win is not something an Aries Sun does easily. You're built to go at things head-on. Mars rules your sign, and the whole point of you is to begin, push, get there first. The Six of Swords is a leaving. Someone picks up a pole and moves the boat off, quietly, while the argument is still going on the bank behind them. On an Aries Sun that can feel like conceding, and I'd guess part of you is cross about it.

The astrology is kinder than it looks. Aquarius, the card's sign, sits a sextile from Aries, two signs apart, which is a cooperative angle, an easy opening you still have to walk through yourself. Air and fire feed each other too, so the thinking this card asks for tends to give you energy instead of draining it. Mercury has no particular dignity in Aries and takes on Mars's colour there, so your mind moves the way your body does, fast and decisive. Once you've decided to go, you really go. The hard part is the deciding, because it means admitting the fight isn't worth what it's costing you.

Usually it's a job. A manager you've been battling for a year, a team where you're always the one pushing, and you realise one morning that all that energy could be landing somewhere useful. It can be a sport or a competitive friendship too, the rivalry that used to be fun and now just leaves you tired. Pick a date for leaving and tell one person you trust, out loud, so it's real.
sun.reversed:
Upside down, the boat stays tied to the bank because you've decided you're not leaving until you've won. An Aries Sun turned against this card digs in out of pride, staying in the job, the flat, the group chat, long after it stopped giving you anything, because leaving would look like losing. The other version is the opposite and just as Aries. You storm off in one afternoon, burn the bridge, and take the whole fight with you into the next place.

Both tend to show up at work first. You'll recognise the colleague you're still arguing with in your head months after you left, or the resignation email sent at eleven at night. With a sibling or an old friend it can be a feud that's been going so long nobody remembers what started it. Before you either stay or go, write down what winning would actually get you, and see whether it's worth another year.

moon.upright:
Feelings in an Aries Moon arrive hot and quick, and you like to think they're gone by morning. This card drawn for your tides says something slower is going on. There are six swords standing in that little boat and nobody is throwing them overboard. The hurt from whatever happened is coming with you, even though you've mostly stopped talking about it.

Mercury picks up Mars's colouring in your Moon's sign, so the mind argues. You lie awake having the conversation you didn't get to finish, and in your version you're sharper and they're sorry. Air feeds fire, which is the problem and the help at once. Thinking about it keeps the anger lit, and it's also how you move through it, since your sign's instinct is to act and this card asks you to let something carry you for a while. The sextile between Aquarius and Aries means the calmer water is genuinely within reach. You don't have to fight your way to it.

Sleep is where it shows first, a restless few nights, a clenched jaw when you wake. Your body wants to move, and it should. A long walk or a hard swim will settle an Aries Moon faster than any amount of talking. With a brother or sister, or whoever you fight with most easily, you might find yourself being unusually patient, and that's the card working. Go for the walk the day after the row, before you text anyone.
moon.reversed:
Blocked, this card on an Aries Moon looks like getting over something at record speed. Two days after the break-up you're fine, you've rearranged the furniture, you've booked a trip. Mars-coloured Mercury tells a good story about how it's all done and dusted. It isn't, and the swords you didn't look at are still in the boat, rattling around.

What it usually turns into is anger in the wrong place. You snap at the friend who's helping, or the person at the checkout, and the sadness underneath never gets its turn. The body carries it as tight shoulders, headaches, a short fuse in traffic. Give yourself one evening to be sad about it on purpose, with nothing to fix and nobody to argue with, and see what comes up.

rising.upright:
Look at the ferryman. He's standing, facing forward, doing the work without fuss, and that's roughly how an Aries rising comes across when this card is drawn for your mask. People meet you mid-move. You've just started somewhere, or you're about to, and you look like someone who's made up their mind.

Mars rules your rising sign, which makes it your chart ruler, and Mercury in Aries takes on that Martian edge. You decide quickly and you say what you've decided in about four words. The sextile from Aquarius opens a door for you, and air feeding fire means new situations catch quickly around you. The tension is that this card is about a leaving that's still a bit sore, and Aries rising doesn't like to be seen hurting. So you walk into the new place brisk and cheerful, and you don't mention the old one.

In a new job it's the first week, when you're already suggesting improvements. After a move it's the new street, the café where they learn your order by the third visit. It can be a new look as well, a haircut after a bad year that tells everyone that chapter is over. When someone asks why you left the last place, give them one honest sentence and then change the subject.
rising.reversed:
The fast start curdles into a habit of starting. Aries rising with this card reversed can be the person who's always new somewhere, new job, new city, new crowd, and who leaves before anyone gets past the first impression. It looks brave from outside. From inside it's often a way of never being known well enough to be let down.

Or it goes the other way and you're stuck on the jetty with your bag packed, telling people you're about to go. Either way the CV tells the story, or the dating history does, lots of good first months and not many second years. Next time you arrive somewhere, stay long enough to find out what people think of you once the novelty has worn off.

sun.upright:
Taurus builds things to stay put, and this card is about packing up and going. That's the whole difficulty in one line. You've put years into whatever this is, a house, a job, a way of doing things, and the card, turning up in your light, says some of it has to be left on the bank. Aquarius squares Taurus. They're both fixed signs, both stubborn, and when they meet there's friction that eventually forces a move.

Air and earth are opposed elements, so this reads like an argument between an idea and a pile of belongings. You can see perfectly clearly that it's time to go. Then you look at everything you'd have to carry and the idea goes quiet for another six months. Mercury is only a visitor in Taurus, coloured by Venus, which means you think best when you're comfortable and you think slowly. There's an older link too. Mercury rules the first ten degrees of Taurus through the Five of Pentacles, the card of being left out in the cold, so this planet knows what hardship feels like in your sign. The Six is the way out of that.

With money it's often a move to something smaller or simpler that you've resisted because it looks like going backwards. At work it's the role you've outgrown and keep because the super is good. At home it might be literal, a lease that ends, boxes in the hall. Make a list of what you'd actually take with you if you went, item by item, and notice how short it is.
sun.reversed:
When this card turns over for a Taurus Sun, you dig in. The situation is plainly finished and you stay anyway, partly out of loyalty and partly because you've paid for it, in money or in years, and walking off feels like wasting all that. Sometimes you do leave but insist on bringing the whole house, every grievance and every piece of furniture, so the new place looks exactly like the old one.

The lease you keep renewing, the relationship that's become a habit, the job with the good parking and nothing else going for it. Your body often knows before you do, a heaviness on Sunday evenings that lifts on holidays. Add up what staying costs you each month, in money and in mood, and put that number somewhere you'll see it.

moon.upright:
A Taurus Moon feels safe among familiar things, the same mug, the same side of the bed, the bakery that knows you. So a card about crossing to somewhere new lands on a tender spot. Even when the place you're leaving hurt you, your body has got used to it, and part of you misses it the way you'd miss an old coat.

The square between Aquarius and Taurus puts two fixed signs at odds. The card's cool, long-distance view rubs against a Moon that knows the world through touch and routine. You might understand that the move is good and still feel homesick for the wrong place. Mercury is a visitor in your Moon's sign and borrows Venus's tastes, so your thoughts calm themselves through the senses. A good meal will settle your thinking faster than an hour of reasoning with yourself.

Sleep is the giveaway. New rooms, new noises, and a Taurus Moon lies awake for a week. Appetite goes up or disappears. With a parent it can be the family home being sold, and feelings about it you didn't expect. Take one ordinary comfort across with you on purpose, the pillow, the tea, the Sunday roast, and keep it going on the other side.
moon.reversed:
Blocked, a Taurus Moon holds on with its whole body. You keep driving past the old place. You still buy the brand your ex liked. The move has technically happened, and emotionally you're sitting on the old jetty with a thermos, waiting for things to go back.

It shows up as comfort you don't really enjoy, the extra glass, the online shopping, sleeping in on days that don't need it. Earth holds on to whatever it's given, and Venus-coloured Mercury would prefer not to think about the unpleasant part at all. Let yourself say to one person what you miss about the old situation, the good parts included, and don't argue yourself out of missing them.

rising.upright:
People usually read a Taurus rising as settled, slow to move, someone who'll still be at the same table in ten years. The Six in your mask position shows you mid-crossing instead, and the people around you notice. You're changing jobs, or suburbs, or the way you dress, and your steadiness makes the change look calm even when it isn't.

Venus rules your rising sign and so rules the chart, and Mercury in Taurus takes on her colouring, so you speak gently and pick words for how they'll feel. The trouble is the square from Aquarius. Two fixed signs, both stubborn, and the friction between them is what finally gets you moving. Air and earth disagree about most things. Your instinct is to test the ground before stepping on it, and this card says step off anyway. You'll feel slightly exposed, like someone breaking in new shoes.

In a job interview you come across as the reliable one who's leaving something for good reasons, and that serves you. Moving house, the new neighbours see a careful, pleasant person carrying boxes and forming opinions slowly. In a new friendship you'll be warm and a bit guarded for the first month. Change one visible thing on purpose, a haircut or a jacket, so the outside catches up with what's already moved inside.
rising.reversed:
Reversed, the calm Taurus rising front becomes a bit of a wall. You look unmoved, people assume you're fine with the change, and inside you haven't left at all. Or you refuse to look like someone in transition, keep the old uniform on, turn up at the old haunts, and people are confused about where you actually are.

At work it's the move you've announced and keep postponing. With friends it's saying you're over something while being very obviously still in it. In the body it can sit as stiffness in the neck and shoulders, the classic Taurus place to hold things. Let one person see the unsettled version, even briefly, and let them help carry something.

sun.upright:
This card belongs to Mercury, and Mercury rules Gemini, so it arrives in your light like the landlord dropping by. The planet is at home in your sign, strong and unforced, and Aquarius, the card's sign, is a trine away, air to air, the easiest angle there is. Leaving, changing, moving on to the next thing, you're good at all of that. For you the real question with the Six of Swords is what you take with you.

Same element on both sides turns the volume up. Thoughts come quickly, one idea leads to four more, and you can talk yourself into a new plan by lunchtime. The risk is that you cross so easily you never look at the swords in the boat. Gemini learns by moving and comparing, and the lessons from the rough water are real ones, about who you trusted and why. If you skip them they tend to turn up again in the next place under a different name.

At work it might be a course, or a sideways move into something that uses your head differently. With a brother or sister it can be the first calm conversation in a while, the two of you agreeing to leave an old argument where it is. Friendships sort themselves too, and there's a group chat you'll quietly mute. Before you go, say to someone the real reason you're leaving, just once, in plain words.
sun.reversed:
The trouble for a Gemini Sun is that talking about leaving can feel almost exactly like leaving. You tell everyone the plan, you research the new city, the course, the flat, and six months later you're in the same place telling people about the plan. Mercury is so strong in your sign that words can do the work of action, and when this card is reversed, they do.

The other version is too much crossing. A new job every year, a new circle, the story of the last place told as a funny anecdote so it never has to be sad. Friends lose track of you. Pick the one move that matters most and give it a date, then stop discussing it with anyone until it's done.

moon.upright:
A Gemini Moon calms down by putting things into words. You feel better once you've told the story, preferably to two or three people, and this card drawn for your tides is Mercury's own card coming home to that habit. Mercury rules Gemini, so what soothes you and what the card is asking for turn out to be the same thing. You get to talk your way across.

Air meeting air amplifies it, though, and you'll know the downside. At night the mind keeps going, rewording the text, replaying the conversation, drafting three versions of what you'll say. The trine between Aquarius and Gemini makes the move toward calm genuinely easy, easier than you'd expect. What gets in the way is the chatter. Grief in a Gemini Moon often comes out as restlessness, flicking between apps, reading the same page four times, and it's easy to miss that it's grief at all.

With a sibling or an old school friend, one long phone call can shift more than a month of thinking did. Your sleep needs some help, a paper book instead of the phone, a walk before bed. At work you might be quietly relieved to be moving desks or teams, lighter than you've felt for a while. Tell the whole story once, start to finish, to someone who'll just listen, and then let it be told.
moon.reversed:
The talking goes round in circles when this card is reversed. You've told the story so many times it's become a routine with a punchline, and the actual feeling hasn't been touched. A Gemini Moon can explain its own hurt beautifully and still not feel it, and that's what this tends to show, a lot of words sitting on top of something quiet and sad.

Look for it at bedtime, the scrolling that goes past midnight, the podcast you need on to fall asleep. Look for it with friends too, when you catch yourself retelling the break-up for laughs. Try saying it once in as few words as possible, a single sentence about what you lost, and leave a silence after it.

rising.upright:
With Gemini rising, Mercury is your chart ruler, and this is a Mercury card, so it lands right on the steering of your whole chart. People meet you as quick, curious, easy to talk to. With the Six drawn for your mask, they meet you in motion, just back from somewhere or about to head off, full of news about the place you're leaving.

Mercury is at home in Gemini, and the trine with Aquarius means the card and your rising sign speak the same language. You'll find new people very easy. The tension is quieter. Gemini rising uses chat as a front door, and a card about leaving something painful asks what's behind the door. People may read you as fine, better than fine, and you'll let them. The calm the card describes is real enough. You're just not advertising the rough water you came through to get it.

Short trips suit this. A commute that changes, a new route to work, a weekend away that resets your head. Starting a new job you'll be the one who knows everyone's name by Wednesday. With neighbours it's easy small talk and a slightly guarded front. When someone new asks how you're doing, try a truer answer than the usual one and see what happens to the conversation.
rising.reversed:
Gemini rising with the Six reversed tends to look like someone permanently halfway out the door. You're charming, funny, you mention the next plan within five minutes, and people come away feeling they didn't quite meet you. The jokes do a lot of work. They keep the conversation away from whatever you're actually leaving behind.

It shows in new jobs where you're liked by everyone and close to no one, and in dating, where the first three messages sparkle and then you go quiet. Sometimes it's a restless sort of stuckness instead, lots of browsing for flights you don't book. At the next introduction, let one question land without making a joke of it.

sun.upright:
There's a woman in this boat with a child pressed against her, and for a Cancer Sun that's the first thing to notice. You're here to protect people and keep a home going, and this card shows someone doing both while leaving. Sometimes the kindest thing you can do for the people you look after is move them, or yourself, away from what's been hurting everyone.

Aquarius and Cancer are five signs apart, a quincunx, which means they have almost nothing in common and have to keep adjusting to each other. The card's instinct is cool and long-sighted, get some distance and think it over. Yours is to gather everyone close and feel it through. Air and water don't clash, but they do have to be introduced. You'll probably feel the pull as guilt, as though leaving were disloyal. Mercury does have a foothold in your sign, though. It rules the middle ten degrees of Cancer through the Three of Cups, the card of friends raising a glass, so your sign knows how to find company and lightness again once this is done.

With family it can be a move, a separation handled carefully, or simply stepping back from being the one everyone rings in a crisis. At work it's often a caring role you've outgrown, the team you've mothered for too long. In the body it tends to sit in the stomach. Make one decision purely for your own sake, and tell the people it affects gently, without apologising for it.
sun.reversed:
A Cancer Sun with this card reversed usually can't leave because someone needs them. The job is bad but the team would fall apart. The house is full of hard memories but the kids' friends are here. Some of that is true, and some of it is a very Cancerian way of avoiding your own fear of the new place. The swords stay in the boat and the boat stays tied up.

Sometimes it's the opposite. You go and take everyone's problems with you, still solving the old family's crises by phone from the new town. Watch for tiredness that sleep doesn't fix. Ask yourself who would actually be harmed if you stepped back, name them one by one, and check the list with someone who'll be honest.

moon.upright:
The Moon rules Cancer, so a Cancer Moon feels everything at full strength, the Moon in its own sign. This card arriving in your tides brings Mercury in Aquarius into the most feeling spot in the chart, and the two signs have nothing in common. They're a quincunx apart. The card wants perspective. Your Moon wants to be held while it cries. Both are right, and you'll probably swing between them.

From inside it feels like homesickness for somewhere that wasn't good for you. You can know that leaving was right and still miss the smell of the old kitchen. Memory is strong in a Cancer Moon, and it edits, keeping the good evenings and dropping the arguments. Air can help here, oddly. A bit of Aquarian distance, thinking about it as if it happened to a friend, gives you somewhere to stand while the feelings move through. You don't have to choose between feeling it and understanding it.

Food and sleep show it first, the comfort baking, the nights you wake at three. With your mother, or whoever mothered you, old patterns may come up, and you might find yourself ringing more often, or hardly at all. At home you'll want to make the new place feel safe fast. Put one familiar thing in the room where you sleep and let the rest of the unpacking wait.
moon.reversed:
The pull back to the old shore is very strong for a Cancer Moon when this card is upside down. You reread old messages. You drive past the house. You tell yourself it's nostalgia, and it is partly, but it's also a way of keeping the grief from ever finishing. The feelings go round in the same little bay and never reach open water.

It shows up at night mostly, and around family occasions, the birthday, the anniversary, the photo that turns up on your phone. You might also shell up and stop telling anyone how you are. Pick one keepsake from the old chapter to keep, and put the rest of it, the messages or the photos, somewhere you have to make an effort to reach.

rising.upright:
Cancer rising meets people from behind a shell, polite and warm and careful, and it takes a while before you let anyone in. Here the shell has come along on a move. You're somewhere new or in the middle of getting there, and what people notice first is how carefully you're looking after everyone else while it happens.

The Moon rules your rising sign, so your chart ruler is the Moon, and your first reactions follow your mood closely. Mercury in Cancer is a visitor, coloured by the Moon, which means your words come out soft and a bit indirect. The quincunx with Aquarius is the awkward part. The card's style is cool, rational, a little detached, and that isn't how Cancer rising likes to be seen. You may come across cooler than you feel, and people could read your caution as coldness in the first few meetings.

In a new workplace you'll be the one bringing biscuits in the second week and remembering birthdays by the third. In a new neighbourhood you'll learn the streets slowly, one familiar walk at a time. With a new partner's family, you'll hang back and watch. Let one person see that you're finding the change hard, early on, instead of waiting until you feel safe.
rising.reversed:
The shell shuts completely. Cancer rising with the Six reversed tends to retreat from new people altogether, so the move happens and then you hide in it, working from home, ignoring the doorbell, keeping the old friends on the phone and making no new ones. Or the move keeps being put off because the thought of all those first meetings is too much.

People read it as shyness or aloofness. At work it can mean you're known as nice but hard to reach. With family it's often you still hosting every holiday back at the old house. Get one small routine going in the new place, the same café on the same morning, so that a few faces start to recognise yours.

sun.upright:
Nobody claps when this boat pushes off. The Six of Swords is one of the quietest leavings in the deck, a hooded figure sitting low, a ferryman who doesn't look back, and a Leo Sun doesn't really do quiet exits. You're here to be seen doing what you do, to put your whole heart into it and have that noticed. So a card that asks you to slip away from something, without the speech, runs against the grain.

Aquarius sits directly opposite Leo, so this card comes from the far end of your own axis. An opposition is a pull toward balance. Leo gives warmth and wants it back personally, and Aquarius stands back and looks at the whole group. Air feeds fire, which helps, since a cooler, wider view of what happened can actually steady you. Mercury has no dignity of its own in Leo and borrows the Sun's colour, so when you think about this you think about it in terms of pride, who saw, who knew, how it looked. That's the bit that makes leaving so hard, the thought of people watching you go.

At work it's the role where you gave everything and got very little back, the boss who never once said well done. In love it can be a relationship where you were the one shining and the other person stopped looking. A creative project might need to be shelved, for a while at least. Tell the people who matter that you're going, keep it to a couple of sentences, and let your next piece of work do the rest of the talking.
sun.reversed:
This reversed, a Leo Sun either refuses to leave because leaving would be a humiliation, or leaves with fireworks. You stay in the job out of pride, or you quit in front of everyone and make sure the whole office hears why. Neither version gets you across. The first keeps you stuck and the second drags the old drama into the new place.

It often shows up in love, the ex you still perform for on social media, the new partner who hears too much about the last one. At work it's the grudge against a former boss that comes up in every interview. Leave one small thing without announcing it, and notice how it feels when nobody makes a fuss.

moon.upright:
After a hurt, a Leo Moon wants warmth, a bit of fuss, and someone to say you deserved better. The Six turning up in your tides offers something cooler. It's the relief of getting away, with the grief still sitting in the boat beside you, and it doesn't come with much applause.

The card's sign, Aquarius, is Leo's opposite. In feeling terms that opposition shows up as a swing between wanting everyone to know how you've been hurt and wanting to be completely above it. Air feeds fire, so talking it through can warm you back up quickly. Mercury is only a guest in Leo and takes the Sun's colouring, which means your thoughts keep circling back to your own dignity. You'll know it by the way you replay the moment you were embarrassed, more than the moment you were sad.

With a partner it may be the first night you sleep properly after a rough patch, and you'll want them to notice how gracious you've been. With children, if you have them, or with the people you look after, you may find yourself being brave for them, and that's lovely, and it tires you. Your heart and your energy rise and fall together, so a lack of rest shows quickly. Let one friend spoil you a little, dinner or a long phone call, and say plainly that you needed it.
moon.reversed:
A Leo Moon with this card reversed tends to wait on the old shore for someone to come and fetch it. You've been hurt, you'd like an apology, and until you get one you're not moving. Pride keeps you standing right where the hurt happened, and you go over it there, again and again.

It shows up at home as a coolness that everyone can feel and nobody's allowed to mention. With friends it's the invitation you decline so they'll notice you're missing. In the body it can feel like a heaviness in the chest that lifts the moment someone makes a fuss of you. Decide that the apology may never come, and do one warm, generous thing for yourself anyway.

rising.upright:
Leo rising walks into a room and people turn to look, and you like it. The Six of Swords as your mask is a lower-key entrance. With Leo rising, Aquarius sits on the cusp of your seventh house, the house of partners and the people you deal with one to one, so this card tends to arrive through someone else. A partner, a business contact or a close friend is making a change, and you're in the boat with them.

The Sun rules Leo, which makes it your chart ruler, and Mercury in Leo borrows its colour, so you speak with warmth and a bit of theatre. The opposition between the signs is the tension. People are used to reading you as bright and confident, and this card gives you a quieter, more reserved look, the one who's thinking something over. Air feeds fire, though, so the change suits you better than you'd guess. Some people will find you easier to approach like this.

At work you might be the calm one during a restructure, the person others go to because you're not panicking. With a partner it's the move you make together, the new city or the new arrangement, and how you present it to everyone else. In your appearance it can be a toned-down season, fewer statement pieces. Let someone else be the face of the change for once and watch how people respond to you when you're in the background.
rising.reversed:
Leo rising reversed with this card can't bear to be seen in the middle of something difficult. So you keep the bright face on, crack the joke, make the entrance, and nobody would guess you're half out the door of a situation that's hurting you. Or you make the leaving itself the show, and people remember the exit far better than anything that came before it.

In partnerships it can be letting the other person carry the whole move while you manage appearances. At work it's the farewell speech that says slightly too much. With friends, watch for the photos posted to prove you're fine. The fix is a small one. Tell one person the less flattering version of what happened.

sun.upright:
Of all twelve signs, Virgo is where Mercury is strongest. It rules the sign and it's exalted there too, so the card's planet is working at full power in your light, the landlord at home with every light on. In Aquarius, the card's own sign, Mercury is visiting someone else's house. In Virgo it knows where everything is kept. So for a Virgo Sun the Six of Swords becomes a very well-planned crossing.

The catch is the quincunx. Aquarius and Virgo are five signs apart and share nothing, so the card's long, detached view doesn't sit easily with a sign that trusts details and checklists. Air and earth pull against each other as well, the idea of leaving against the practical proof that it will work. You'll feel it as wanting certainty before you move. You'll have the spreadsheet, the timeline, the backup plan, and still hesitate, because the card is asking you to go on a sense of direction and a bit of faith. There's a Mercury decan in your sign too, the Ten of Pentacles in the last ten degrees, which is family, inheritance, what lasts. You want whatever you build on the other side to hold.

At work this is often a move you've been designing for months, a new role, a transfer, a business of your own. With health it can be leaving behind a routine that wore you down and starting a gentler one. With a parent or older relative it might be practical help with their move. Pick the one piece of information you're still waiting for, decide you can go without it, and set the date.
sun.reversed:
Reversed for a Virgo Sun, the planning becomes the place you live. There's always one more thing to research, one more risk to cover, and the boat sits at the jetty fully provisioned for a crossing that never starts. Mercury is so strong in your sign that the mind can keep itself busy forever. Or you do go, and spend the whole time correcting what went wrong at the old place.

Watch for it at work, where you've become the person who fixes the department you meant to leave. Watch the body too, a tight stomach and bad sleep before any decision. Choose one thing on your list that doesn't have to be perfect, do it at seventy per cent, and move on.

moon.upright:
A Virgo Moon settles by sorting things out. When you're upset you clean the kitchen, fix the spreadsheet, reorganise the cupboard, and somewhere in the middle of all that the feeling gets a bit smaller. This is a Mercury card arriving in your tides, and Mercury is at its strongest in Virgo, ruling and exalted, so your usual way of calming down is exactly what helps this time.

Where it rubs is the element. Air and earth are opposed, and the card's cool, reasoning distance meets a Moon that feels things in the body. You can think through the whole situation very clearly and your stomach still won't settle. The quincunx between Aquarius and Virgo adds its own awkwardness, a sense of constant small adjustments, nothing quite fitting. Worry is the usual form grief takes in a Virgo Moon. It looks like fretting about small practical things while the big sad thing sits unexamined.

Your digestion and your sleep will tell you how it's going. Routines help, the same walk, the same bedtime, meals at proper hours. With a close friend you might find yourself being the helpful one when you could do with some help yourself. At work, a tidy handover or a clean inbox can bring genuine relief. Once a day, stop fixing for ten minutes and let yourself feel whatever's under the lists.
moon.reversed:
The worry won't switch off. A Virgo Moon with this card reversed goes over the same details again and again, what you said, what you should have said, whether you packed the charger. The mind that usually calms you keeps checking instead, and it's exhausting.

Look for it in the body first, a tense gut, a tight jaw, lying awake making lists. You might also criticise yourself for not having recovered quicker, as if grief should run to a schedule. At home it's the cleaning that never quite finishes. With the people close to you it can come out as nitpicking. Write the worries on one page, then close the notebook and leave it in another room overnight.

rising.upright:
Mercury rules Virgo, so with Virgo rising it's your chart ruler, and it's exalted in your rising sign as well. When a Mercury card lands in your mask position the whole chart pays attention. People meet you as competent, careful, clearly thinking. With the Six there, they meet you as the person who knows how to get from here to there, and they'll often ask you to help them do it.

The quincunx with Aquarius makes it a slightly awkward fit. The card's style is broad and a little detached, and Virgo rising prefers to be seen getting the details right. Air and earth rub, the plan against the practical reality. You might come across as quieter than usual, a first impression that says capable and slightly elsewhere. The upside is that people feel safe around you when things are changing. They can tell you won't lose the paperwork.

In a new job you'll be the one who's read the handbook. Helping a friend move, you'll bring the labels and the tape. When you meet new people there's a kind of quiet helpfulness that makes them trust you quickly. Let someone else do the organising once, even if it's done worse, and see how it feels to arrive somewhere as a passenger.
rising.reversed:
With the card reversed, Virgo rising can look like it has everything handled while the move quietly stalls. You're organised to the eyeballs, answering everyone's questions about the change, and still not actually going anywhere. Or the helpful front wears thin and people see the anxiety underneath, the over-explaining, the apologising.

It shows at work as busyness that doesn't move anything forward, and with new people as a stiffness that's hard to get past. Your posture may give it away, shoulders up, jaw set. A friend might notice you've started answering their questions with a plan when all they asked was how you are. Next time you're introduced to someone, skip the explanation of what you're doing and why, and just ask about them.

sun.upright:
Libra wants things to be fair, and nothing about the situation this card is leaving was fair. That's usually what makes the leaving so hard for a Libra Sun. You'd like to go in a way that's balanced and civil, everyone understanding, nobody hurt, and this card is a bit more lopsided. Someone has to pick up the pole and go while the other side is still unhappy.

The good news is in the astrology. Aquarius and Libra are both air signs, a trine apart, the easiest link there is. The card speaks your language. You're good at the cool, reasonable conversation this card needs, the one where you explain calmly why things have to change. Same element can amplify too, though. Two air signs together can talk forever, weighing it up, getting everyone's view, and never quite push off. Mercury is a visitor in Libra and takes on Venus's colour, so your thinking leans toward keeping the peace.

Most often this is a relationship, or a partnership at work. A business arrangement that's become one-sided, a flatmate situation, a marriage where you've done all the adjusting. It can also be a legal or contractual matter being settled, and a clean agreement is something you're very good at drafting. Write the one sentence you'd say if you didn't have to be nice about it, and use a kinder version of that sentence.
sun.reversed:
A Libra Sun with the card reversed often stays because leaving would upset someone. You weigh it and weigh it. There's always a good argument on both sides, which is the curse of seeing everyone's point of view, and so the boat stays at the jetty while you wait for a leaving everyone will agree to.

Watch for it with a partner, where you keep adjusting to keep the peace and lose track of what you actually want. At work it's the role you keep for the sake of the team. You may also leave and then spend months smoothing things over with the people you left. Pick one decision where someone will be disappointed in you, make it, and let them be disappointed.

moon.upright:
Tension in the air is the thing a Libra Moon finds hardest to live with. An argument in the next room, a friend who's gone cold, a household where everyone's walking on eggshells, and you feel it before anyone says a word. The Six of Swords in your tides describes the relief of getting away from that atmosphere into somewhere quieter.

Venus rules Libra, and Mercury in your Moon's sign takes on her colouring, so the mind wants to soothe and smooth. The trine with Aquarius means distance comes to you fairly naturally, which is lucky, because you need it. What you might not expect is the guilt. A Libra Moon often feels that having peace while someone else doesn't is somehow unfair, and you catch yourself checking on the people you've left. Air on air amplifies the thinking, so the relief and the second thoughts can both be loud.

At home it's a calmer house, maybe a new one, where you notice for the first time how tense you'd been. With a partner it's the first easy evening after a hard stretch. Your sleep improves when the noise stops, sometimes almost straight away. With friends you might want to pull back from anyone who brings drama. Let yourself enjoy the quiet without ringing to check that everyone else is all right.
moon.reversed:
When this card turns against a Libra Moon, you can't settle until everyone's happy, and they won't be. So you keep going back across the water to mediate, to explain, to make sure nobody's upset with you. It's kind, and it keeps you in the rough part.

You'll find it at family gatherings, where you're still the go-between. You'll find it at night, when you rehearse a conversation to make it perfectly fair. Your body may register it as a low headache or tight shoulders. A friend who always brings drama may need to be seen less often. The next time you feel the urge to smooth something over, wait a day first, and see whether it sorts itself out without you.

rising.upright:
People meet a Libra rising and find you easy company, agreeable, well put together, good at putting others at ease. With this card as your mask you're doing all that in the middle of a change. People read it as grace under pressure, the one who left a bad situation and was polite about it.

Venus rules your rising sign, so she's your chart ruler, and Mercury in Libra borrows her manners. You're tactful. You say the difficult thing nicely. The trine with Aquarius means the card's clear-headed style suits you, and you come across as fair and reasonable about something that might have been ugly. The only tension is that same element on same element can make you look a touch too composed, and people might not realise how much it cost you.

In a new job you'll make friends quickly, and people will trust you with the diplomatic stuff early. Meeting a new partner's friends, you'll be charming about your past without giving much away. At a work event you'll be the one who manages to say something kind about the former employer, and people will remember it. In how you look there might be a refresh, something softer. When someone new asks about the old situation, tell them one true thing about how hard it was.
rising.reversed:
Libra rising reversed with this card can mean the pleasant front has turned into a way of avoiding the move. You're lovely to everyone at the old place, you haven't said you're leaving, and every day you don't say it makes it harder. Or you've gone, and you're so gracious about it that nobody knows anything was wrong, including, sometimes, you.

It shows up in networking, the polite nothing-answers about why you changed jobs. In relationships it's the break-up you've let drift because saying it would be unkind. Say the plain version once, to the person who most needs to hear it, and let the politeness come after.

sun.upright:
Scorpio doesn't leave things by halves. When you're done, you're done, and the other person tends to find out by how completely you've gone. The Six of Swords leaves differently. It's slow, it's carrying the pain openly, and it doesn't burn the jetty on the way out. For a Scorpio Sun that's an unfamiliar way of going.

Aquarius squares Scorpio. Both are fixed signs, both dig in, and the friction between them is the kind that eventually forces action. Air and water are neutral to each other, so the card's cool thinking and your deep feeling have to be introduced before they can work together. Mercury is a visitor in Scorpio, coloured by Mars and, for modern astrologers, Pluto, which gives your mind a sharp investigative edge. You want to understand exactly what happened and who's responsible before you go. The card asks you to go before you have every answer.

At work it might be leaving a place where you were betrayed, or where the power games wore you out. In a relationship it's the ending that's taking its time, the separation that has to be done properly, money split, belongings divided. It can also be a family secret you're finally stepping away from. Leave one question about what happened unanswered, on purpose, and see whether you can still move.
sun.reversed:
Reversed on a Scorpio Sun, the crossing stalls because you can't let it go. You want to know why, you want it acknowledged, and some part of you wants them to pay. So the boat sits in the middle of the water while you keep looking back at the shore.

The other form is the clean cut that isn't clean. You block the number, delete the photos, never mention them again, and carry the whole thing in silence for years. It tends to surface in work disputes and in old family matters. Your sleep may be light and your temper short. Tell someone you trust the full story once, including the part where you were hurt, which is usually the part you skip.

moon.upright:
Grief goes deep in a Scorpio Moon and it goes quiet. You don't cry in public. You probably don't cry much in private either, at least to begin with. What this card in your tides shows is the feeling being carried, hooded and silent, the way the passenger in that boat sits with her head down, and actually moving somewhere.

The square between Aquarius and your Moon's sign is two fixed signs locking horns. Aquarius wants to step back and look at it objectively. Scorpio wants to feel every part of it and understand what it meant. Air and water don't mix naturally, so the card's coolness can feel like being asked to stop caring. It isn't that. Mercury, coloured by Mars and Pluto in your Moon's sign, makes your thinking intense and private, and a bit suspicious. You'll go back over the details for clues.

In intimate relationships this can be a slow recovery of trust, one honest conversation at a time. Sleep might be full of vivid dreams while your mind sorts things out underneath. Your body may feel heavy and slow for a while, and that's fine. With money shared with someone else, a settlement or a split, keep things in writing and keep them calm. Tell one person the thing you haven't told anyone, and choose them carefully.
moon.reversed:
Blocked, the feelings go underground. A Scorpio Moon with the Six reversed can hold a grudge, or a grief, for a very long time without mentioning it to a soul. You look calm. Underneath you're still on the old shore, going over what happened, sometimes checking up on people you've supposedly left behind.

It shows up late at night, scrolling through an ex's profile or rereading an old argument. It can show in the body as tension you can't place. Jealousy can flare over something small. Choose one thing you've been keeping tabs on, stop checking it for a month, and notice what you feel when the urge comes.

rising.upright:
Scorpio rising gives off something intense and private, and people sense there's more going on than you're saying. With this card in your mask position, what they sense is a person who's come through something difficult and isn't going to explain it. You look composed, a bit closed, and quietly determined to get to calmer ground.

Mars rules Scorpio traditionally and Pluto in modern charts, so one or both are your chart ruler, and Mercury in Scorpio takes on their colour. Your words are few and pointed. The square from Aquarius adds friction. The card's style is open and detached, yours is guarded, and people may feel the gap. Air and water have to be introduced, and a new group might take a while to warm to you. You'll be watching them closely in the meantime. Some people find that magnetic. Others find it a little unnerving.

Starting a new job, you'll size everyone up within a day and tell no one what you've concluded. After a move, the neighbours will find you polite and hard to read. In a new relationship there's a slowness to trust that the other person will need to respect. Let one new person in on a small, true detail about your past early, before they have to earn it.
rising.reversed:
The guard goes all the way up. Scorpio rising with the Six reversed can look impenetrable, cool and watchful, and people assume you're either hostile or hiding something. Usually it's neither. You're just still braced from what you left, and your face hasn't caught up with the fact that you're somewhere safer.

At work this can come across as suspicion of new colleagues, or a reluctance to share information. With new friends it's the three-month test nobody knows they're sitting. In dating it can look like interest followed by a sudden withdrawal the moment things get personal. Try smiling first at the next person you meet, before you've decided anything about them.

sun.upright:
Leaving is something a Sagittarius Sun can usually do with a spring in its step. New country, new course, new people, you're built for the horizon, and Jupiter, your ruler, likes things big and hopeful. So a card about moving on should suit you, and in one way it does. Aquarius sits a sextile from Sagittarius, a friendly angle that opens a door, and air feeds fire, so the idea of somewhere better lights you up quickly.

The complication is Mercury. It's in detriment in Sagittarius, the sign opposite its home, so the card's planet works against the grain in you. Mercury likes detail, the map, the timetable, the list of what to pack. Sagittarius likes the view from the top of the hill and trusts the rest to sort itself out. So your version of this crossing can be a bit rushed and underplanned, and the swords you're carrying don't get looked at because you're already talking about the next place. Mercury also rules the first ten degrees of your sign through the Eight of Wands, which is speed itself, things flying through the air. You're good at quick. The Six is slower than that, and it has a sadness to it you might want to skip.

It can literally be travel, a move overseas, a job in another city. It can be study, or leaving a belief system or a teacher you've outgrown. With friends it might be leaving a group whose values you no longer share. Before you go, sit down with the practical side, the bills, the dates, the addresses, all the tedious Mercury stuff, and get someone detail-minded to check it.
sun.reversed:
The reversed Six on a Sagittarius Sun can turn escape into a lifestyle. Every time something gets hard there's a flight, a new plan, a fresh start somewhere with better weather, and the old trouble quietly packs itself into your luggage. From outside it looks adventurous. You know it's a bit of running.

The other version is a trip that won't happen, the visa that stalls, the course you enrol in and defer twice. Either way, look at the places you've left, jobs, cities, friendships, and what they had in common when you went. Write down the last three exits and the reason for each, and see which reason keeps turning up.

moon.upright:
Optimism is how a Sagittarius Moon copes. You look for the funny side, the lesson, the silver lining, and you usually find one. What the Six of Swords shows in your tides is the sadness that sits underneath the cheerfulness, travelling with you whether you mention it or not. You'll still be telling jokes, and they'll be good ones.

Mercury is in detriment in your Moon's sign, which means the words for feelings come out too big or too breezy. You say it was all for the best before you've really felt that it was. Jupiter rules Sagittarius and inflates whatever it touches, so relief feels like euphoria one day and the grief feels bottomless the next. The sextile from Aquarius does help. A bit of distance comes naturally to you, and air feeds fire, so talking to someone wise can lift you right back up.

You'll want to move your body, long walks, a run, a drive with the windows down. Being outdoors helps a Sagittarius Moon quickly. With a friend who's known you for years, a long honest conversation might reach the part of it you've been joking about. Plans for travel can be a real comfort too. Book something small and nearby, a weekend somewhere with a view, and let yourself be quiet while you're there.
moon.reversed:
Blocked, a Sagittarius Moon outruns its own feelings. You're busy, you're planning, you're cheerful in a slightly frantic way, and the grief keeps trying to catch up. When it does, usually late at night or in an airport, it lands all at once. Jupiter's optimism is a real gift, and here it's being used to skip a chapter.

You might notice it in how much you're drinking or how often you're booking things. With friends there's a lot of big talk about new beginnings. Sleep can be restless, with a sense of needing to be somewhere else. Pick one evening a week with no plans at all, stay home, and let whatever's been chasing you arrive.

rising.upright:
Sagittarius rising comes across as open, funny, a bit restless, the person who's just back from somewhere or about to go. With this card as your mask, people meet you mid-crossing and assume it's another adventure. Sometimes it is. More often there's something you're getting away from, and you're choosing not to lead with it.

Jupiter rules your rising sign and so rules the chart, and it tends to make you look confident and generous whatever's going on underneath. Mercury is in detriment in Sagittarius, so your first words are warm and a little imprecise. You'll say yes to things before you've read the fine print, and you might tell a new person a bit too much or not quite enough. The sextile from Aquarius opens doors socially, and with air feeding fire you pick up new friends quickly on the other side.

At a new job you'll be liked quickly and trusted a little later, once they see you finish things. In a new city you'll find the good pub, the good walk and three new friends within a month. With a partner, the move might be your idea and your energy, and they'll need to see a plan as well as a vision. Take the boring admin seriously for once, and let people see you do it.
rising.reversed:
Sagittarius rising with this card reversed can look like someone who's always leaving. The stories are great, the plans are big, and people slowly realise you never stay long enough for anyone to know you well. Or you're stuck somewhere you've clearly outgrown, bored and a bit tactless about it, and everyone can see you'd like to be gone.

It shows at work as enthusiasm at the start of things and drift in the middle. In friendships it can be a pattern of drifting off without saying goodbye. With a partner it might be the promise of a trip that keeps being made and never booked. Before your next move, have one proper goodbye conversation with someone who mattered at the place you're leaving.

sun.upright:
Capricorn leaves the way it does everything else, with a plan, a timeline and a clear idea of where it's going. That's no bad fit for this card. Saturn rules your sign, and Saturn is also the traditional ruler of Aquarius, the card's sign, so the Six comes from a neighbour who answers to the same landlord. The two signs sit side by side, a semi-sextile, neighbours with little in common who each have what the other lacks.

What Aquarius has that you lack is detachment from the scoreboard. You tend to measure the move by where it gets you, the title, the salary, the reputation, and the card is more interested in getting away from something that's been hurting you. Air and earth are opposed, the idea against the proof, and you'll want proof. Mercury has no dignity of its own in Capricorn and picks up Saturn's colouring, which makes your thinking careful, dry and a bit pessimistic. You'll assume it'll be harder than it is. Sometimes that's useful. Sometimes it keeps you in a job two years longer than you needed to be there.

Work is the obvious place, leaving a firm or a role you've climbed through, possibly for something that looks like a step sideways. With a parent it might be stepping out from under their expectations. In the body, Capricorn tends to hold tension in the knees and back, and this kind of transition can show there. Write down the reason you're going in one line, and when doubt comes, read it again instead of redoing the plan.
sun.reversed:
A Capricorn Sun with the Six reversed tends to stay out of duty. You made a commitment, people rely on you, and leaving would look irresponsible, so you keep carrying a situation that stopped carrying you years ago. The other version is the cold exit, a clean, well-managed departure that leaves the feelings completely unaddressed, which works fine until they turn up at the next job.

Watch the working hours, the weekend emails, the sense that rest has to be earned. With family it may be a role you've held since you were young, the responsible one. Give yourself a date by which you'll decide, and treat it like any other deadline you'd never miss at work.

moon.upright:
Capricorn Moons cope. That's the pattern. Something hard happens and you get on with it, sort the paperwork, keep turning up, and the feelings are filed for later. The Six of Swords in your tides describes the later, the grief that's come with you across the water, sitting quietly in the boat while you steer.

Saturn rules your Moon's sign and is also the old ruler of Aquarius, so there's a familiar sternness in how this card lands. Mercury picks up Saturn's colour here, and your thinking about feelings can be very practical, sometimes harsh. You might tell yourself you should be over it already. The semi-sextile between the signs means they don't share much, and air and earth pull in opposite directions, the reasonable story against what your body is still holding. Capricorn Moons often feel grief physically, as tiredness or a sore back, long before they'd call it sadness.

Work is where you'll hide, and it's also where the relief shows first, a job that's a little less stressful and suddenly you're sleeping better. With a parent, old patterns about being the strong one might surface. In your routine, the things that help are structural, a regular bedtime, a proper lunch, a walk at the same hour. Let one person see you tired, without explaining or apologising.
moon.reversed:
When the card is reversed, a Capricorn Moon holds everything in and keeps working. The move happened, you managed it well, and you haven't felt a thing about it, or so you say. Saturn's colouring makes it easy to call this discipline. The feelings don't go anywhere, though. They go into your shoulders.

You'll find it in the long hours, the reluctance to take leave, the dry jokes that deflect any question about how you're doing. At home you might be short with people for no reason you can name. Sleep can mean early waking, lying there at four thinking about work. Book a day off with nothing in it, and don't fill it with jobs around the house.

rising.upright:
Capricorn rising looks capable. People meet you and assume you've got it handled, and usually you have. With the Six of Swords as your mask, they meet you in the middle of a well-managed exit, and it looks deliberate and dignified, a professional leaving a situation that wasn't working.

Saturn rules Capricorn, which makes it your chart ruler, and it's the traditional ruler of Aquarius too, so this card and your rising sign share a boss. Mercury, coloured by Saturn in your rising sign, makes your words measured and dry. You say what's necessary and very little else. The semi-sextile means the card's cool, forward-looking side and your practical front are next door to each other without being close. Air and earth rub. People may read you as a little cold about the change, when in fact you've thought about it for months.

In a job interview this is a strong look, the candidate who left for sound reasons and says so briefly. With new colleagues you'll come across as reliable and a bit reserved. In your appearance it might be something sharper, a better coat, a more serious haircut. Tell one new person what you're hoping for from the move, as well as what you're leaving behind, so they see more than the competence.
rising.reversed:
Capricorn rising with this card reversed can hide a stalled move behind a very convincing front. You look like someone who's on their way, you talk like someone with a plan, and you're still in the same office. Or you've left and you're so buttoned up about it that people find you hard to approach.

It shows up in networking as a list of achievements with no story attached. At work it might be taking on more responsibility at the old place instead of leaving it. Your posture can tighten, the jaw and the shoulders set. Let someone at the new place see you make a mistake early and laugh it off.

sun.upright:
This is one of your own sign's cards. It's the middle decan of Aquarius, Mercury ruling the degrees from ten to nineteen, so if your Sun sits there it's your birth decan, and even if it doesn't, this card is native to your sign. It speaks the way you think, calm, a step back, looking at the whole thing from a little distance.

Same element on both sides amplifies it, for better and for too much. The better is that you're genuinely good at this crossing. You can leave a bad situation without drama, think clearly about what went wrong, and point yourself somewhere saner. Mercury is only a guest in Aquarius, coloured by Saturn and, in modern charts, Uranus, which makes the mind steady and original. The too much is that Aquarius is fixed air, and fixed signs can hold an idea for a very long time. You might have decided to leave years ago, in your head, and never told your body.

In friendships and groups, which matter a lot to you, this can be stepping back from a crowd whose values have shifted. Your working life could shift toward something more independent, or more useful to more people. With a partner, it can be the calm talk about what needs to change. Your sign's own Major is The Star, the card of hope after a storm, and this card is the road there. Tell one friend what you've decided, and let them ask you how you feel about it.
sun.reversed:
The detachment that usually serves an Aquarius Sun can turn cold with this card reversed. You leave, you move on, you're fine, and the people you left are baffled by how little it seemed to cost you. Sometimes it didn't cost you much. Often it did, and you just put it somewhere you don't visit.

The stuck version is the fixed-air one, a decision to leave held as a principle for years and never acted on. Look for it in groups and friendships that feel stale, and in a partner who says they can't reach you. Ask yourself what you felt the day you decided to go, and say that feeling out loud to someone.

moon.upright:
An Aquarius Moon needs room. When things get heavy you step back, get some air, think about it from a distance until it makes sense, and only then do you feel ready to come back and talk. This card is from your own sign, the second decan of Aquarius, so what it describes in your tides is your usual method working well. You're putting some water between yourself and the upset, and it helps.

Air on air amplifies it, and the cost is that thinking can stand in for feeling. You can understand exactly why something hurt and still not have let it hurt. Mercury in your Moon's sign is coloured by Saturn and Uranus, cool and a little unpredictable, so the feelings tend to arrive late and sideways, a flash of sadness in the middle of a normal afternoon, weeks after the event. Being fixed, an Aquarius Moon also holds its emotional conclusions tightly once it's reached them.

Friends are central for you, and one or two will probably be the ones who help you across, the ferryman with the pole, so to speak. With a group you belong to, you might need a break. Sleep is often fine and then suddenly not. Your nervous system can feel buzzy, as if a wire is humming. When one of those late, sideways feelings arrives, stop what you're doing for five minutes and let it be there.
moon.reversed:
Blocked, an Aquarius Moon goes numb. You're perfectly pleasant, perfectly reasonable, and you've quietly stopped feeling much about anything. The Six reversed shows the swords still in the boat and you looking the other way, discussing them intelligently as though they were someone else's.

It shows up with friends as a coolness they can't quite name, and with a partner as a sense that you're watching the relationship from the next room. Sometimes it goes the other way and you keep going back to the old situation to analyse it. Do something physical and a bit silly with a friend, dancing badly in a kitchen or a swim in cold water, and notice what comes up.

rising.upright:
Aquarius rising meets people with a friendly, slightly detached air, interested in them and hard to pin down. This card comes from your own rising sign, the second decan of Aquarius, so in your mask position it looks entirely natural. You come across as someone who's left something behind with very little fuss, cool, clear, and already thinking about the next thing.

Saturn is your traditional chart ruler and Uranus the modern one, and Mercury in your rising sign takes their colour, so you're articulate, a bit unusual, and not easily rattled. Same element amplifies it. The composure can be real, and it can also be a very good cover. People who meet you in this phase will have no idea there was rough water. That's partly because you've processed it and partly because you'd prefer not to discuss it with strangers, which is fair enough.

In new groups you'll be the one with the interesting idea and no personal history on display. At a new job you'll be seen as calm under pressure, possibly as a little aloof. In dating you'll be good company and slow to open up. Let someone see a trace of the old shore, a sentence about what you left and why, so they have something human to hold on to.
rising.reversed:
The friendly distance hardens with the card reversed. Aquarius rising can become unreachable, polite to everyone, close to no one, a person who seems to have moved on so completely that there's nothing to connect with. Or you're so busy being different from the place you left that people only ever meet the reaction.

It shows in new workplaces where you're respected and not really known, and in friendships that stay at the level of ideas. It can also look like stubbornness, a fixed stance about the old situation that won't take any new information. Your style might change sharply, as if to prove the break. Ask someone new a personal question, and answer it yourself as well.

sun.upright:
Water is your element, and this card is a picture of a crossing over water, so there's something in it a Pisces Sun recognises straight away. The drift, the quiet, the sense of being carried. What's harder is the planet behind it. Mercury is in both detriment and fall in Pisces, as far from home as it gets, which means its usual method, list, plan, reason it out, simply doesn't work in your sign.

So this card asks a Pisces Sun to leave something without a clear reason you could write down. You know you have to go. You couldn't explain it in a meeting. Mercury in Pisces has to learn your sign's way of knowing, which is by feel, by dream, by the mood of a room, and that's the real lesson here. The semi-sextile between Aquarius and Pisces makes them neighbours with little in common, and air and water are neutral, so they have to be introduced. The card's cool distance can feel alien. It's also exactly what you need, since you tend to absorb everyone's pain and carry it as your own.

Often this is leaving a situation where you've been a sponge for someone else's trouble, a partner in crisis, a friend who only rings when things are bad, a job in a caring field that's drained you. In a creative life it might be letting go of a project that stopped being yours. Sleep and dreams can be vivid and useful. Before you decide anything, take a day near water, the beach or a river, and notice what you already know by the end of it.
sun.reversed:
Drift is the risk for a Pisces Sun with this card reversed. The boat isn't tied up and it isn't going anywhere either, just turning slowly in the middle of the water while you wait for a sign. Mercury is so weak in your sign that decisions can feel impossible, and it's tempting to let circumstances decide for you.

The other form is escape, the move that's really a disappearance, into a new town, a new relationship, a lot of wine or a lot of sleep. Look for it in the plans you describe as fate. Pick one practical step in the direction you already sense is right, the phone call or the form, and do it before the mood changes.

moon.upright:
A Pisces Moon picks up everything, the tension at the dinner table, the friend's bad week, the sadness on the train. So a card about moving away from turbulent water is, for you, often about moving away from other people's storms, the ones you've been feeling as if they were yours.

Mercury is at its weakest in Pisces, in detriment and fall, and in your Moon's sign that means the mind can't really help you sort the feelings. You try to think it through and it goes soft and circular. The card's Aquarian distance is foreign to you, since the signs are neighbours with little in common, and air and water need introducing. Still, a little distance is what's being offered, and taking it doesn't make you heartless. Jupiter, and Neptune in modern charts, rule your Moon's sign, and both make boundaries hazy. This card is asking for one, gently.

Sleep will probably be deep and full of dreams, some of them about the old place. With a partner or close friend, you might need to step back from being their emotional support for a while. Music, water, time alone near the sea or in a bath, all of these help. When you feel low, ask yourself whose feeling it is before you decide what to do with it.
moon.reversed:
When a Pisces Moon can't make the crossing, it tends to sink into the old sadness and stay there. Feeling it becomes a place to live. You play the songs, reread the letters, and let the mood set the whole day, and because Mercury is so weak in your Moon's sign, there's not much inner voice saying enough.

It also shows as taking on everyone else's rough water again, the friend in crisis, the family drama you're pulled back into. Sleep might be too much or broken. Escape can creep in, too many screens, too much wine. Choose one boundary, one person you'll stop rescuing for a while, and tell them kindly.

rising.upright:
Pisces rising meets the world softly. You look gentle, a bit dreamy, easy to confide in, and people tend to tell you things within ten minutes. With the Six as your mask, they meet you in a quiet, drifting kind of transition, someone who's left something and seems to be floating toward the next thing without much fuss.

Jupiter is your traditional chart ruler and Neptune the modern one, both generous and hazy. Mercury, in detriment and fall in your rising sign, makes first conversations warm and imprecise. You forget names, you lose the address, and people forgive you because you're lovely. The card's cool Aquarian style is a neighbour you don't have much in common with, and air and water don't naturally mix, so on some days you seem calm and on others lost, and neither is quite accurate.

At work you'll be the one people bring their problems to, and that can drain you quickly if you're still recovering yourself. In a new relationship you'll be tender and a bit vague about your past. After a move, you'll find a favourite quiet spot early, a park bench or a window seat. When someone new starts leaning on you, say that you're settling in and can't take much on, and leave it at that.
rising.reversed:
Pisces rising, with the card reversed, can blur into the background. You're so accommodating in the new place that nobody knows what you actually want, or you've drifted into a situation because someone else steered and you didn't say no. People might see you as lost, or as someone who's always about to leave.

It shows at work as saying yes to everything, and in love as a pattern of being rescued, or rescuing. There can also be confusion about the move itself, forms not filled in, dates missed. Get one person who's good with details to sit with you for an hour and make the practical part concrete.

1.upright:
The first house is the body you walk around in and the way you start things, the front door of the chart. It's also where Mercury has its joy, the house where it traditionally does its best work, so a Mercury card landing here is well placed. What's live is how you carry yourself through a change. You're leaving something, or you've just left, and it shows in your face, your posture, the way you introduce yourself.

The first house's natural sign is Aries, ruled by Mars, and Aquarius sits a sextile from it, a cooperative angle that still needs you to act on it. Fire and air help each other here. Your thinking gets quicker and clearer as you move, and moving helps you think. Because the first house is angular, a corner of the chart, whatever happens in it is visible. People will notice you've changed before you've told them anything. The tension is that the card still has swords in the boat. You can look fresh and brisk and be carrying a fair bit of sadness underneath.

In the body it might be sleep improving, a return of appetite, the first run in months. In how you present yourself it can be a new haircut, a different way of dressing, a tidier desk. With new people, you'll find yourself introducing a slightly different version of yourself, less defined by what happened. Pick one small physical habit that belongs to the new chapter, a morning walk or a different route, and keep it going.
1.reversed:
In the first house the stuck crossing shows on you. You look tired, or tense, or braced, and people ask if you're all right when you thought you were hiding it well. Mercury's joy is here, so the mind is lively, and it's lively in circles, rehearsing the same exit without ever taking it. Or you've rushed into a new look and a new attitude that doesn't quite fit yet.

It tends to show in the body first, tight shoulders, a jaw that aches when you wake, shallow breathing. It can also show in how you start things, lots of beginnings abandoned. Pick the one change you've been talking about making and take the first physical step, the booking or the form, and let the rest follow.

2.upright:
Money and what you think you're worth sit in the second house, the actual bank balance and the actual sense of whether you deserve more. The Six landing here usually means a financial crossing. You're moving away from an arrangement that's been costing you, a job that underpaid, a debt, a shared account that stopped being fair, toward terms that let you sleep.

The house's natural sign is Taurus, and Aquarius squares it. They're both fixed signs, so this is a slow, stubborn friction between an idea about money and the money itself. Air against earth is the plan on paper against what's in the account. You'll feel it as knowing exactly what you should do, cancel the subscription, ask for the raise, move the savings, and finding that the knowing doesn't shift anything by itself. Because the second house is succedent, it's about building up and holding, so the change here is gradual. You'll likely be carrying some cost from the old situation for a while.

On the job side, expect a pay conversation, or a move to a job that pays less and costs you less in every other way. At home it can be a budget redone from scratch, or selling something you've held on to. Your sense of worth may take longer to catch up than your bank balance. Write down the one number that would tell you the crossing is done, and check it every few months.
2.reversed:
Stuck money is usually what this looks like in the second house. You know the arrangement isn't working, the overdraft, the loan to a friend that never comes back, the joint account with an ex, and you keep putting off dealing with it. Or you leave one financial mess and walk straight into a new one with the same shape, because the habit came along too.

The square between the signs makes it stubborn. Look for it in automatic payments you've never cancelled and in the reluctance to open certain emails. Your self-worth can drag too, a sense that you don't deserve better terms. Sit down with the actual figures for an hour, with someone you trust if that helps, and close one account or one agreement that belongs to the old shore.

3.upright:
Mercury is the natural ruler of the third house, so this card is on home ground here. The third is everyday talk, messages, siblings, the neighbourhood, short trips, the things you're learning. With the Six drawn into it, what's live is a change in how you talk and who you're talking to. Conversations that used to be hard are getting easier, or you're finally having the one that lets you move on.

Aquarius and Gemini, the house's natural sign, are a trine apart, both air, so the flow is easy. Same element can overdo it, though. You might talk about the move endlessly, text every friend, research every option, and find that the words keep you busy while nothing actually changes. Cadent houses are about processing and adjusting, and the third house processes by talking. That's useful, up to a point. The swords in the boat are real ones, words that were said, and you'll want to say something back.

With a brother, sister or cousin, this can be a calmer way of speaking after years of the same argument. Your commute or the short trips you take might change, a new route, a new town nearby. If you're studying, it can be dropping a subject that wasn't working and picking one that is. Send the message you've been drafting, in its shortest version, and then leave the reply to them.
3.reversed:
Words that won't get said, or words that won't stop, are how this looks in the third house. You keep rewriting the same message. You go over an argument with a sibling or a neighbour again and again in your head. Since Mercury rules this house, the mind is strong, and turned against itself it becomes a loop.

It shows in the phone, the drafts folder, the group chat you've muted and still read. It can show on short trips too, the drive you keep putting off, the visit you cancel. Learning can stall as well, a course abandoned halfway. Choose one conversation that's been stuck, say what you need to say in three sentences, and stop there.

4.upright:
The fourth house is home in every sense, the actual house or flat, the family you grew up in, and the private ground you go back to when you close the door. The Six here is usually about moving that ground. It might be literal, packing up and leaving a place, or it might be a change in how you relate to your family, stepping back from an old role at the kitchen table.

Cancer is the house's natural sign, and Aquarius and Cancer are five signs apart, a quincunx, which means constant small adjustment with nothing in common to lean on. Air and water have to be introduced. In practice the card's cool, practical view, this place isn't working, let's go, sits awkwardly against the fourth house's attachment to memory and belonging. You can know the move is right and still find yourself standing in the empty room longer than you meant to. Because the fourth is angular, the change is visible and decisive. Other people will see it happen.

With parents it can be a shift from looking after them to letting others help, or from being looked after to standing on your own. With the house itself, it's the practical crossing, the boxes, the bond, the last walk through. With whoever you live with, there's often a quieter atmosphere once the move is made. Keep one object from the old place that holds a good memory, and give it a proper spot in the new one.
4.reversed:
A home that won't let you go is the usual picture in the fourth house. The lease is up and you renew. The family pattern you swore you'd leave keeps turning up at every gathering. Or you've moved, and the new place feels like a waiting room because you've never really unpacked.

Look for it in the boxes still taped shut, the family group chat that sets your mood for the day, the childhood room you still sleep in when you visit. Sometimes it's a parent's home you can't stop managing from a distance. The quincunx keeps things awkward and unresolved. Unpack one room completely, hang something on the wall, and let the new place start to be yours.

5.upright:
Fun, romance, creative work and children all live in the fifth house, the part of life that's meant to be enjoyed. A crossing card here usually means joy is coming back after a stretch when it went missing. Something that used to be a pleasure turned into a strain, a relationship, a hobby that became an obligation, and you're leaving that behind for something lighter.

Leo is the house's natural sign and Aquarius sits right opposite it, so this card comes from the far end of the axis.
